plan: Hold the workspace dictionary behind a deep-copy boundary: deepcopy on construction and again in to_data(), so callers can never alias internal state.

Provide a single recursive generator _walk() yielding (item, containing_list, depth) in document order; it drives word counting, marker collection, outlining, and id lookup so there is exactly one traversal to get right.

Use per-kind contribution dispatch: notes contribute words from their text after compiled-regex marker stripping (markers replaced by a space so they never fuse adjacent words), and contribute marker identifiers; references contribute their declared word_count and unresolved list; containers contribute nothing directly.
Render outline() from the walker's depth values: workspace title unindented, then two spaces per nesting level followed by '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check string-typed ids, resolve the item and its containing list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, reject self/descendant destinations via an identity-based subtree scan, and bounds-check the index (0..len inclusive) — all before touching the tree; only then remove by identity and insert/append, so any ValueError leaves to_data() byte-identical.

Ship an in-memory unittest suite (stdlib only) covering totals, marker sorting/dedup, outline text, reordering and reparenting moves, every rejection path, and workspace invariance after each failed move.
mechanisms: single recursive (item, parent_list, depth) walker shared by all queries
per-kind contribution dispatch for notes vs references
compiled marker/word regexes with space-substitution stripping
validate-then-mutate move protocol with identity-based containment and removal
